exposure: mode of delivery (elective cesarean section, natural vaginal delivery)
cohort: A total of 350 women who had either an elective cesarean section or natural vaginal delivery at least three years prior were included in the study.
finding: The study observed a higher prevalence of metabolic syndrome in women with a history of elective cesarean section (30.29%) compared to those with natural vaginal delivery (18.29%).
mod_finding: Multivariate logistic analysis revealed that natural vaginal delivery was significantly associated with a decreased likelihood of metabolic syndrome (Adjusted OR: 0.57, P = 0.04) after adjusting for age and breastfeeding duration.
